newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil INPC inflation index at 0.60 pct - IBGE.
newsitem.headline: Brazil INPC inflation index at 0.60 pct - IBGE.

text.p: Brazilian inflation in April as measured by the National Consumer Prices Index (INPC) was 0.60 percent, down from 0.68 percent in March, the National Statistics Institute (IBGE) said in a statement.
The INPC is based on the spending of families earning up to eight minimum salaries.
The Wider Consumer Prices Index (IPCA), which measures the spending of families earning up to 40 minimum salaries, was up at 0.88 percent against 0.51 percent the previous month, the IBGE said.

April's results mean the INPC index over the last 12 months was 8.20 percent, down from 8.55 percent in the 12 months to the end of March, while in the case of the IPCA, the 12-month index was 8.58 percent in April compared with 8.99 percent in March, the IBGE said.

The main sectors driving INPC inflation in April were communications, up 37.54 percent on March, root vegetables, up 7.49 percent and domestic fuels, up 7.34 percent, the IBGE said. ((-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
